newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-LEHMAN FRUSTRATED BY OPENING ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEHMAN FRUSTRATED BY OPENING ROUND.

text.p: - Tom Lehman felt frustrated and angry with himself after he began the defence of his British Open title with a three-over-par 74 at Royal Troon on Thursday.
The titleholder and winner of the Loch Lomond World Invitation last Saturday felt he could, and should, have done better.
"I'm a little frustrated and a little bit angry at the way I played," said the American. "The back nine was tough but I hit only one green in regulation.
"I made a bunch of bogeys and I can do better than that."
Lehman played the front nine well enough with birdies at the fourth and fifth to go with seven pars.
However, along with so many others on the inward nine, he suffered in the headwind and he felt his swing did not hold up in the conditions.
"It didn't feel so good today. I wasn't happy with the way I was swinging," he said.
"I hit the ball very unsolid which is unusual for me and that's why I struggled so much. I didn't hit many greens because I was hitting it off-centre most of the time."

Five bogeys on the back nine wrecked his card and left him seven shots off the pace. "That's as tough a back nine as there is anywhere," he said. "There are really about five par fives on the back nine which is a par of about 41."

Lehman denied that the pressure of defending his title had affected his game, saying: "Being the defending champion is wonderful but once Thursday gets here it's a new Open and you can't live off last year's championship or anything else, reputations or whatever.
"You've got to put the ball on the tee in play and it's a whole new year.
"That's a thing of the past now and I'm concentrating solely on this year."
